title: PE Thrombectomy
summary: Mechanical clot removal for selected acute pulmonary embolism with clinical deterioration or high-risk features.

items: High-risk PE with shock, particularly when thrombolysis is contraindicated or unsuccessful.
Clinical deterioration despite anticoagulation: consider with PERT/attending.
RV strain and elevated troponin/BNP inform risk, not automatic thrombectomy eligibility.
Not routine for stable low-risk PE or clot size alone.

items: Inability to tolerate therapeutic anticoagulation or active major bleeding: individualized PERT/attending decision.
Recent intracranial hemorrhage or intracranial surgery: major anticoagulation risk; require neurosurgical/PERT review, not an automatic exclusion from rescue mechanical thrombectomy.
Uncorrectable coagulopathy or severe thrombocytopenia.
No safe venous/right-heart route or device-incompatible anatomy, including relevant valve prostheses or intracardiac hardware.
Continue therapeutic anticoagulation per PERT/attending; confirm current agent and last dose before IV heparin.
Mechanical thrombectomy does not replace anticoagulation; use the adult VTE protocol in Pre-procedure orders.
Large-bore access increases bleeding risk. Intracranial bleeding/surgery requires an individualized anticoagulation plan.
Thrombolysis contraindications are not identical to mechanical thrombectomy contraindications.
Platelets >50,000/µL.
UFH anti-Xa target: 0.3-0.7 IU/mL.
NPO (if moderate sedation).
Vital signs per routine.
PIV placement.
Glucose POC.
Baseline CBC, PT/INR, aPTT, and BMP/creatinine; document actual body weight.
Continuous ECG and pulse oximetry; oxygen and hemodynamic support as indicated.
80 units/kg IV bolus, then 18 units/kg/hour; use local dose caps/nomogram.
adjust or omit bolus as directed; do not automatically re-bolus.
anti-Xa or aPTT at 6 hours and after dose changes; CBC/platelets and subsequent checks per protocol.
no heparin with HIT or heparin allergy. Recent Xa inhibitors affect anti-Xa testing; confirm assay with pharmacy.
heparin/ACT dosing per attending and device protocol.
local anesthesia with minimal/moderate sedation as tolerated.
general anesthesia when necessary; induction/positive-pressure ventilation may worsen RV failure. Coordinate an airway/hemodynamic rescue plan.
CTA clot location, RV strain on CT/echo, and venous access/right-heart anatomy.
confirm results meet procedure-specific requirements when indicated; see the Labs tab.
confirm tolerance; review active bleeding, recent intracranial hemorrhage/surgery, HIT/allergies, and last anticoagulant dose.
review the planned method, ability to lie flat/tolerate procedural positioning, and NPO status if sedation/anesthesia is planned. Coordinate rescue support with PERT/anesthesia.
Penumbra or Inari system, compatible access, and monitored inpatient bed.
thrombectomy and procedure-specific risks.
Pulmonary embolism thrombectomy.
Bleeding.
Infection.
Damage to nearby structures.
Pulmonary artery injury/rupture, hemoptysis, or significant aspiration blood loss.
Arrhythmia, valve injury, cardiac perforation/tamponade, or hemodynamic collapse/death.
Incomplete clot removal, recurrent embolism, or need for further intervention.
Contrast reaction or kidney injury.

items: femoral vein to IVC and right atrium; jugular access is an alternative.
right atrium through tricuspid valve, RV outflow tract, and pulmonic valve into the main pulmonary artery.
main PA divides into right/left and then lobar/segmental arteries; match the target to CTA.

right PA runs more horizontally and generally lower, behind the ascending aorta/SVC and anterior to the right main bronchus. Left PA courses posteriorly and superiorly over the left main bronchus; confirm takeoff angles on CTA/angiography.
tricuspid apparatus, RV wall, and distal pulmonary arteries; avoid force and deep wire advancement.
acute obstruction raises RV afterload; sedation or instrumentation can precipitate collapse.
review CTA/echo, confirm target and anticoagulation, and establish a PERT rescue plan.
use ultrasound; establish access compatible with the selected system.
under fluoroscopy and ECG monitoring, guide a catheter from RA through tricuspid valve, RV outflow tract, and pulmonic valve into the PA; avoid force or unsupported stiff wire advancement.
record PA pressure and obtain limited angiography as tolerated; confirm a stable, safe wire position in the intended branch.
advance the selected Penumbra or Inari system per device instructions and attending guidance; monitor blood loss and hemodynamics.
recheck flow, PA pressure, and clinical response; avoid chasing every distal clot. Remove devices, achieve hemostasis, and hand off anticoagulation.
minimize right-heart manipulation; stop and reposition for sustained ectopy or resistance.
avoid deep or forceful wire advancement; hemoptysis or sudden hypotension needs urgent assessment.
avoid excessive sedation; have airway, vasopressor, and rescue support ready.
track aspiration losses, maintain a closed system, and monitor large-bore access.
prioritize clinical/hemodynamic improvement over a perfect angiogram.
confirm ongoing therapeutic anticoagulation and evaluate the DVT source.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: Diet - if no further intervention is planned: Outpatient: order regular diet. Inpatient: notify primary team diet is okay.
Vital signs per monitored-unit routine.
Continuous telemetry and pulse oximetry.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.
Monitor access-site color, bleeding, and swelling.
Continue therapeutic anticoagulation.

blocks.title: Access care
items: Bedrest 2 hours with leg flat.
If a suture device (e.g., woggle) is placed, remove on PPD1.

blocks.title: Disposition
items: Monitored inpatient bed; ICU for instability or ongoing support needs.

blocks.title: Follow up
items: Clinic follow-up interval per MD preference.
